11. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan, learned advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioners took me to the revisional-4 application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, the disposition of all the P.W.s and D.W.s and the documents exhibited by the parties and submits that the plaintiffs as well as the Government miserably failed to prove that the suit land vested in the Government as khas land during the S.A. operation in view of the fact that neither the plaintiffs nor the Government adducted any minimum iota of evidence including the khas khatian itself before the courts below in support of their contention nor did they disclose the source through which or the basis on which or the manner in which the suit land devolved upon the Government and as such the plea of khas khatian which is the genesis of the plaintiffs' claim falls flat and therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan drew my attention to Section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and referred to the decision of Geeta Rani alias Shamima Khatun vs. Bangladesh, 36 DLR (AD) 225; Bangladesh and others vs. Mallick Ali Ahmed and others 3 CLR (AD) 345 and Md. Kalam Mollah and others vs. Sheikh Samsu and others, 23 BLT 320, which will be discussed later on. 

 13. Mr. Zakir Hossain Bhuiyan further submits that the plaintiffs as well as the defendant Nos.1-4 (the Government) did not neither specifically deny the accuracy or genuineness of R.S. Khatian No.259 (Exhibit-1/Ka of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) nor did they take any step against the said R.S. Khatian prepared and published in the name of Satish Chandra Das and as such the same has got presumptive value of correction in view of the case of Government of Bangladesh and others vs. Mrs. Mohsina Rahaman alias Joya as reported in 50 DLR 186, wherein it has been held that : 

 15. Mr. Bhuiyan next submits that the defendant-petitioners have lawful right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the strength of their and their predecessors registered sale deeds dated 22.02.1961 (Exhibit-1 of Title Suit No.154 of 2000), sale deed dated 15.06.1982 (Exhibit-5 of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) and sale deed dated 16.07.2000 (Exhibit-3 of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) and those registered sale deeds being documents of title, will prevail over the so-called and non-existent S.A. khatian mysteriously prepared in the name of the Government. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan placed reliance on 18 BLC (AD) 44; 13 MLR (AD) 6; 32 (DLR) 252; 5 MLR 374. In the case of Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan and others vs. Md. Nasir Hossain and others, 18 BLC (AD) 44, our Appellate Division unanimously held that: 

 17. Mr. Bhuiyan goes on to submit that the lower appellate Court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure justice in failing to appreciate that Plot No.185 was present/included in R.S. Khatian No.259 and as such the observation that the said plot is missing in the khatian is patently perverse and totally contrary to the record of the case. 

 24. Mr. Shah Hossain next submits that the S.A. Khatian prepared and published in the name of the Government vis-à-vis the suit land shall be presumed to be correct unless and until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. In this connection Mr. Hossain referred to Section 19(3) and 144A of the SAT Act and the decisions reported in 9 MLR (AD) 82; 30 DLR (SC) 81; 6 BLC 241; 33 DLR 126; 17 BLC (AD) 174 and 61 DLR 18. 

 Mr. Shah Hossain finally submits that the learned trial Court wrongly shifted the burden of proving the correctness of S.A. Khatian on the plaintiff-opposite parties, and the appellate Court below as the final Court of fact arrived at a proper decision upon proper assessment of the pleadings of the parties, evidence and other materials on ' record and as such the same does not call for any interference from this Court. 

 25. I have meticulously gone through the revisional application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, evidence led by them and other materials on record and also heard the learned Advocates for both the sides at length and perused the decisions relied upon by both the parties with utmost circumspection and the relevant provisions of law wherefrom it transpires that the preparation and publication of S.A. record of rights, if any, in the khas khatians of the Government as well as the maintainability of Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 are the predominant issues in this case apart from other connected issues and I will endeavor to address all the issues in proportion to their respective weight and importance. 

 26. It is the case of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-2 and the Government (defendant Nos.1-4) that the suit land vested in the Government as khas land during the S.A. operation, but neither the plaintiffs nor the Government adduced any evidence including the khas khatian itself before the Courts below in support of their contention. Again, although the Government filed a written statement, they did not adduce any evidence, oral or documentary, to show as to when, why and how the suit land became khas in their name and as such the written statement of the Government will not ipso facto be admissible in evidence unless and until the same is supported by competent witness of convincing nature, and as such Section 92 of the SAT Act as well as the decisions referred to by the defendant: petitioners will stand in the way of the claim of plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-2 as well as the Government.  Secondly, it is as clear as broad daylight from R.S. Khatian No.259 (Ext.l of Title Suit No.154 of 2000) that R.S. Plot No.185 is present in the .said khatian showing 37 decimals of land in sixteen annas share. On this point the learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos.1-2 submits that the said finding is merely a slip of pen on the part of the lower appellate Court and in fact the appellate Court below meant R.S. Khatian No.148 (Ext. 1/Ka of Title Suit No.154 of 2000). On scrutiny of R.S. Khatian No.148, it is found that Plot No.285 appears therein, but the quantum of land in the said plot is completely different, namely 15 decimals in eight annas share. Moreover, lands of both the R.S. Khatian being Nos.259 and 148 belonged to Zaminder Satish Chandra Das and as such I find it difficult to accept the submissions advanced from the plaintiffs on this point. Rather, I subscribe to the view that the Court of appeal below wrongly recorded the said finding as to R.S. Khatian No.259 and Plot No.185 upon his total non-application of judicial mind to the materials on record, which is very unbecoming and deplorable on the part of a judicial officer. 

 31. It appears from paragraph 3 of the plaint that the plaintiffs entered into the suit land after the flood of 1988 whereas they allegedly took settlement of the same in 1999 and they did not at all clarify in their pleadings submitted and evidences adduced in any of the suits in what capacity they possessed and enjoyed the suit land for the intervening period between 1988 and 1999 and as such I am constrained to hold the view that the plaintiffs entered into the suit land as -mere trespassers. Moreover, I think that if the suit land had ever been recorded in the khas khatian of the Government, it would have settled the same in favour of anyone one else, and in the absence of any such lease, government's title to the suit land is not proved at all and therefore, the claim of the plaintiffs also fails since they are claiming interest in the suit land through the Government.
